task.description: Evaluate whether a spacecraft arriving at Jupiter's system at 20 km/s (relative to Jupiter) could realistically use Jupiter's moons to perform a gravity-assist deceleration maneuver (slowing down to enter orbit), and whether that would save a significant amount of propellant compared to chemical braking.
task.target_quantity: Achievable delta-v (deceleration) obtainable from a single moon flyby vs. the delta-v required to be captured at Jupiter; corresponding propellant saving (fraction or kg) and a yes/no on 'significant' + realistic strategy.

internal_prior.note: PRIVATE INTUITION SKETCH — reference input only, never evidence. Its only permitted later use is a divergence-check vs the Node 2b verified result (flag as internal_prior_divergence if large).
internal_prior.sketch: Gravity assist on a massive body exchanges momentum with that body. A flyby changes the probe's velocity VECTOR in the moon's rest frame by rotating it through the deflection angle, with the speed-magnitude in the moon frame UNCHANGED (classic two-body elastic encounter). The deceleration relative to Jupiter comes from the fact that the moon itself moves around Jupiter at v_moon, so the encounter can 'borrow' (or shed) that orbital momentum. The maximum delta-v shed per flyby is bounded by roughly 2*v_moon in the ideal head-on/collinear limit (the moon's own orbital velocity is the fuel). Galilean moon orbital speeds are ~1-2 km/s (Ganymede ~1.4 km/s), far below the 20 km/s approach. So a SINGLE moon flyby can shave off only on the order of a few km/s, not the full 20->capture delta-v. Even stacked, several flybys each give a few km/s. Intuition: moon-assist is a partial, not a complete, substitute for chemical capture; it is realistic only as a fuel-saving complement, and 'significant' depends on how much of the capture delta-v one can attribute to moon encounters vs the residual chemical burn. Expected dominant cost: the chemical delta-v needed to go from 20 km/s hyperbolic approach to a capture orbit is of order 10+ km/s, so a few km/s of assist saves a modest fraction, not most, of the propellant.
internal_prior.dominant_regime: two-body gravity-assist (impulsive) momentum exchange; bound ~2*v_moon per encounter; moon orbital speed is the limiting resource
internal_prior.expected_order: a few km/s total deceleration available from Galilean moon flybys, vs ~10-15 km/s chemical capture delta-v; propellant saving is a fraction, not the majority, of the capture cost; verdict likely 'useful but not sufficient / not the dominant strategy'.

template_adaptation_notes.template_mechanism: Built around AERODYNAMIC DRAG: a body descending through a spatially-varying medium (atmosphere) whose density/temperature couple into the ODE via rho(z), CD, A. Governing force = g_eff(z) - drag(v, rho(z)). Mechanism keyword = medium-coupled viscous deceleration.
template_adaptation_notes.this_problem_mechanism: TWO-BODY GRAVITY-ASSIST: impulsive gravitational deflection of a point-mass probe by a moving point-mass moon; no medium, no drag, no spatially-varying density. Governing physics = conservation of speed in the moon's rest frame (elastic two-body encounter) + the moon's own orbital velocity as the momentum reservoir. Deceleration relative to Jupiter comes from vector rotation through the encounter, magnitude bounded by ~2*v_moon.
line_by_line_instantiation_check: atmosphere-drag-ode step 1 (obtain T(z)/rho(z) as ODE input) - NOT INSTANTIATED: this problem has no medium; the model input is a set of orbital constants (a, M, P of the moons) and the capture-orbit target, not a spatially-varying field array. Dropped.

atmosphere-drag-ode step 2 (Mach thresholds / CD / A piecewise regimes) - NOT INSTANTIATED: no fluid, no transonic band, no drag coefficient. Dropped entirely (this is the '张冠李戴' trap - reusing CD/A values for a gravity problem would be exactly that failure mode).

atmosphere-drag-ode step 3 (ODE dv/dx = g - drag(v,rho)) - NOT INSTANTIATED: the governing equation here is NOT a drag ODE but a closed-form two-body encounter: v_post = R(theta) v_pre in the moon frame, speed |v| preserved, delta-v relative to Jupiter = vector difference. Replaced with the two-body formula.

atmosphere-drag-ode step 4 (ODE integration / solve_ivp) - NOT INSTANTIATED: no integration needed; the result is an algebraic/analytic bound on delta-v from the encounter geometry. Replaced with a direct analytic + closed-form bound computation.

atmosphere-drag-ode step 5 (boundary gate: CD->0 pure gravity, CD->inf stop, mass->0/inf) - PARTIALLY REUSABLE: the 'check degenerate limits' discipline transfers (here: deflection angle ->0 gives zero assist; approach distance -> moon radius gives max deflection ~90 deg; probe mass ->0 gives the classic elastic limit). Adapted, not copied - the specific degenerate limits differ because the mechanism differs.
atmosphere-drag-ode step 6 (conclusion w/ traceability badge) - REUSABLE: keep the traceability-badging discipline.
template_adaptation_notes.verdict: NO EXISTING TEMPLATE FITS - mechanism genuinely different (viscous medium coupling vs impulsive two-body gravity). internal_prior_divergence_check.internal_prior_expected: moon-assist sheds only a few km/s (intuition used moon orbital speed ~1-2 km/s, e.g. 'Ganymede ~1.4 km/s'), vs ~10-15 km/s chemical capture -> saving a modest fraction (10-30%), verdict 'partial, not dominant'.
internal_prior_divergence_check.verified_result: Galilean-moon orbital speeds are actually 8.2-17.3 km/s (Io fastest at 17.33 km/s). Io's single-flyby bound = 24.51 km/s EXCEEDS the 15.59 km/s requirement -> 100% coverage, propellant saving ~99%. Even Callisto covers 75%.
internal_prior_divergence_check.divergence: LARGE. The intuition under-estimated moon orbital speeds by ~10x (1.4 vs 17.3 km/s for the relevant comparison, and 1.4 vs 8.2 for Callisto). The pipeline's use of real ephemeris a-values (421700-1882709 km) caught this: v_moon = sqrt(G_J/a) with actual a gives 8.2-17.3 km/s, not ~1.4.
internal_prior_divergence_check.disposition: The verified computation is trusted over the intuition; the divergence is EXPLAINED (wrong order-of-magnitude intuition for Galilean-moon orbital speeds, not a model bug). No model-form rollback needed - the formula v_moon=sqrt(G_J/a) is standard and was dimensionally + boundary-gated. Intuition corrected; no systemic pipeline bias detected.
